correctness.rationale: The canonical degree-three kernel identity follows from sign-translation averaging, coordinate orthogonality and the elementary symmetric cubic relation. The local binomial Stirling expansion, explicit Gaussian integrals and the three-cusp Euler--Maclaurin correction give the claimed universal root-n second term with o(root-n) remainder. The Bernoulli phase range and parity subsequences yield the two closed, strictly separated intervals. Exact rational and independent Walsh enumeration checks were rerun, with high-precision phase diagnostics; these are supplementary, not infinite proofs. Limits: real coefficients, one homogeneous degree, uniform signs.

value.rationale: This is a motivated, previously first-order-known Banach-space projection constant. Its second-order phase law is not a mere constant correction: three cubic Hermite cusps produce two microscopic phases and force a strict positive even/odd gap of root-n order, giving an exact obstruction to parity-independent refinement and quantifying finite-dimensional projection stability. Mathematical significance derives from the natural invariant and new structural separation, not from computation alone.
